*Sitting down, thinking about the year ahead...*

Ai, let me think about this year. I've been working this land for over thirty years now, so I know what it will do and what it won't do. My wife helps me, and my boy comes back from the construction site sometimes, but most of the year it's just the two of us in the field. We've got 22.5 mu, not a lot but enough if we don't waste anything.

Most of the land, about 15 mu, I do the same thing every year — wheat in the winter, then maize right after. That's how everyone around here does it and it's what works. The other land I split up: about 3 mu for cotton, 2 mu for peanuts, 1.5 mu for millet, and 1 mu for mung beans. The millet and some of the peanuts we eat. The cotton and the rest we sell.

**For the wheat**, I'll plant in mid-October, right after the maize comes out. I buy one bag of that compound fertilizer — the one they call san-ge-shiwu, fifteen-fifteen-fifteen — for each mu and spread it when I plow. Then in spring when the wheat wakes up and starts greening, I go back with urea, maybe half a bag per mu. That's what my father did and that's what I do. I water three times: once before the cold sets in, once at greening, and once when it's filling the grain. Well water is expensive with the electric pump, but if I skip the winter watering the wheat won't make it if it's a dry year. I don't buy fancy seed — I keep some from last year and buy a little from the co-op to mix in. If I see weeds in spring I spray the yellow can of herbicide, one time usually. Normally I get about 400 kg per mu. A good year maybe 450. 2018 I got 500 but that year the rains came right.

**For the maize**, as soon as the wheat combine leaves the field, I have three days, four at most, to get the maize in. No time to plow — I pay the guy with the no-till seeder, 20 yuan per mu, and he puts the seed and the compound fertilizer down together. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, Xianyu or Zhengdan, whichever the shopkeeper has. When the maize is knee-high I go back and scatter urea between the rows. If the summer rains are good I don't water at all. If July is dry I water once, maybe twice. Usually I get 450-500 kg per mu. That bad year, 2020, it was only 350 — I remember because I had to borrow from my brother for winter fertilizer.

**For the cotton**, this is the crop that eats my time. I plant end of April after the ground warms. I put the compound fertilizer down when I plow, then urea when the plants are growing fast. Cotton has many enemies — the bollworm, the red spider — so I spray maybe five, six times through the summer. My wife doesn't like the spraying, it makes your head hurt. We pick in three rounds starting in September, that's the hardest work of the whole year, your back doesn't recover. If I get 250 kg of lint per mu I'm happy. Prices have been bad some years so I keep cotton small.

**For the peanuts**, I plant them end of April. They don't need much — peanuts make their own fertilizer somehow, that's what the old men say. I put down a little compound fertilizer and that's it. Don't usually water. Get about 200 kg, sometimes more. We keep some for oil pressing and sell the rest.

**For the millet**, same time as peanuts. Almost nothing goes into it. No water, barely any fertilizer. It survives on its own. Get maybe 150-180 kg per mu, but it doesn't cost me anything and my wife uses it for porridge all winter.

**For the mung beans**, I plant after I finish the maize, around end of June. They grow fast, finish before the cold. Very little work. We sell at market or give to relatives — a good crop for relationships.

All together, seed, fertilizer, spray, pumping water, hiring the seeder man — probably 11,000 yuan for the year. If the weather behaves, we do alright. If not, we tighten up.
